title: Iterator

act2.summary: a reverse traversal (most recent first, reused by three reports) and a bounded forward scan that must stop once it has enough matches, both reported against how many entries were actually visited

solutions.title: The log is iterable; nothing outside it does page arithmetic
solutions.tradeoff: Every report reads as a plain traversal instead of a page/offset double loop. The price: ObservationLog now owns the one and only place that walks pages, so a genuinely new traversal order still means opening that file, not just the caller's.

reviewFocus: Do allMessages/lastEntries/findFirst still know pages exist after the refactor, or do they only see entries?
Does the new reverse traversal reuse ObservationLog's own page structure, or does a caller reconstruct paging arithmetic by hand?
Is `scanned` in the act 2 functions counting real work (entries actually visited), or is it decorative on top of an eager implementation?
Is the walkthrough honest about how close this act 2's numbers are between the two routes, and about why (see ACT2.md)?
Does `[Symbol.iterator]` get used directly (for...of, spread), or does the solution route reintroduce a hasNext()/next() protocol GoF itself only describes as one option?
